# Harrison

## Overview

- **Gender:** Male  <sub>[v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Origin:** New Brunswick  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Role:** Farmer  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** a crank  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Appearance

He is a fussy, fidgety, and crusty little man. He sits on his vine-shaded veranda enjoying his pipe in his shirt sleeves.

_Sources: [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)_

## Personality

Mr. Harrison is eccentric, outspoken, and quick-tempered, believing strongly in telling the disagreeable truth to others regardless of their feelings. He keeps to himself, dislikes unnecessary fuss or traditional domestic routine, and maintains an unhurried, irregular schedule for meals and housework. Despite his crusty, sharp, and cynical exterior, he possesses a soft spot for good company, appreciates youthful spirits, and can be mild, friendly, and neighborly once his temper cools.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P7](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0007), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P46](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0046), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005), [v2 c9 P6](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0006)_

## History

In April, Mr. Harrison purchased Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea next to the Cuthbert place, bringing along his foul-mouthed parrot Ginger. He quickly acquired a reputation in the village as an eccentric crank due to his peculiar solitary housekeeping, irregular meal hours, and outspoken criticism of local gossipers. After an initial confrontation with Anne Shirley over a straying cow, he felt ashamed of his temper and welcomed her into his home when she arrived to apologize for selling the animal by mistake. The two shared tea and quickly formed a warm, unlikely friendship, with Mr. Harrison expressing interest in the Avonlea Village Improvement Society. He frequently hosted Anne on his veranda for conversations where they debated frankness, human nature, and community matters. In local newspaper gossip, he was jokingly rumored to be pursuing romance, though he actually only visited neighbor Harrison Andrews to play checkers.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P4](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0004), [v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005), [v2 c1 P6](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0006), [v2 c1 P8](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0008), [v2 c3 P1](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0001), [v2 c3 P3](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0003), [v2 c3 P16](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0016), [v2 c3 P39](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0039), [v2 c3 P46](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0046), [v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049), [v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000), [v2 c9 P6](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0006), [v2 c24 P2](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0002), [v2 c24 P5](../source/v02-c24.md#nw-v02-c24-p0005)_

- Originally from New Brunswick before moving to Avonlea  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>
- Bought Mr. Robert Bell's farm in Avonlea adjoining Green Gables  <sub>[v2 c1 P5](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0005)</sub>

## Quotes

> It was the truth and I believe in telling the truth to everybody.  <sub>[v2 c9 P5](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0005)</sub>

> I’m a crusty, lonesome, crabbed old chap, but there’s something about that little girl makes me feel young again . . . and it’s such a pleasant sensation I’d like to have it repeated once in a while.  <sub>[v2 c3 P49](../source/v02-c03.md#nw-v02-c03-p0049)</sub>

> That old nuisance of a Rachel Lynde was here again today, pestering me for a subscription towards buying a carpet for the vestry room. I detest that woman more than anybody I know.  <sub>[v2 c9 P0](../source/v02-c09.md#nw-v02-c09-p0000)</sub>
